confidence_scale.SUPPORTED: a focused experiment confronted an explicit prediction
confidence_scale.STRONGLY_SUPPORTED: repeated or independently correlated evidence is protected by an executable gate

entries.observation: The old flag/poll ordering admits a signal-after-test-before-poll lost-wakeup window. The replacement blocks SIGINT/SIGTERM before creating signalfd, polls that descriptor with the listener, and completed 64 CTest plus 128 evidence-collector stress iterations.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; the static counterexample window exists and the chosen wait set removes that specific ordering. No timeout was added.
entries.interpretation: The correction follows from signal-mask and file-descriptor event semantics; repetition checks the implementation but is not the correctness proof.
entries.learning: For this single-threaded Fedora/Linux probe, signalfd provides one race-free event source for blocked shutdown signals and listener activity.
entries.candidate_rule: A blocking RF-A0 wait must have an atomic relationship with shutdown notification; lost-wakeup-prone flag-plus-wait designs are rejected.
entries.governance_consequence: RF-A0.SIGNAL.CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN and RF-A0.SIGNAL.STRESS protect the correction.
entries.open_question: Other signal/lifecycle requirements of a real SisTer service remain unverified.

entries.observation: The run recorded Fedora Linux 44 Workstation, kernel 7.1.6-201.fc44.x86_64, x86_64, and glibc 2.43 alongside its toolchain.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; all required identity fields were available through read-only inspection.
entries.interpretation: Distribution, kernel, libc, architecture, and project behavior are separate provenance dimensions.
entries.learning: RF-A0 evidence is a Fedora reference-platform observation of Linux interfaces, not evidence that every distribution or kernel behaves identically.
entries.candidate_rule: Every decisive RF-A0 run records the actual Fedora/userspace/kernel/libc/toolchain baseline and bounds conclusions to it.
entries.governance_consequence: RF-A0.PLATFORM.FEDORA and RF-A0.PLATFORM.COMPLETE are machine-readable gate checks.
entries.open_question: Which observations remain stable on another Fedora release or Linux userspace is not yet known.

entries.observation: GCC 16.1.1 compiled with -std=c++23 and warnings as errors; the probe enforced and reported __cplusplus=202302. No new standard-library dependency was needed.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; CMake metadata, compile command, successful build, and probe report agreed.
entries.interpretation: Accepted language mode is directly evidenced; complete C++23 standard-library conformance is neither required nor established.
entries.learning: C++23 is the application language contract, while Linux/POSIX calls remain direct experimental interfaces and library capability claims stay facility-specific.
entries.candidate_rule: Record compiler/version, actual command, requested mode, accepted language macro, and exact library facilities relied upon.
entries.governance_consequence: RF-A0.TOOLCHAIN.CXX23_COMMAND and RF-A0.TOOLCHAIN.CXX23_ACCEPTED enforce the contract.
entries.open_question: No unused C++23 library facility needs qualification at RF-A0.

entries.observation: commitment.json recorded protocol digest cba33a... at 16:47:56Z; observation.json began at 16:48:00Z, carried the same digest, and the gate rehashed the unchanged protocol.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; commitment preceded decisive observation and digest linkage validated.
entries.interpretation: The evidence establishes ordering inside this orchestrated run, not authorship, originality, truth, or ignorance of earlier observations.
entries.learning: Separating protocol and synthesis plus committing exact bytes gives a mechanically auditable but deliberately narrow temporal epistemic boundary.
entries.candidate_rule: Every decisive run must persist a protocol digest before observations and carry it through observation and ledger validation.
entries.governance_consequence: RF-A0.EPISTEMIC.PROTOCOL, DIGEST, and ORDER enforce separation and ordering.
entries.open_question: External timestamping or authorship attestation is outside RF-A0 and not implied.

entries.observation: Static AST inspection found subprocess creation only in execution_authority.py; its policy and implemented roles matched, shell execution was absent, and every executed action carried a role and constrained argv.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; direct project-script authority was centralized and default-deny with argument-shape checks.
entries.interpretation: This bounds commands directly launched by project Python, while CMake's compiler/linker children remain an explicit delegated build boundary.
entries.learning: Effect-oriented control requires constraining executable identity and arguments, not merely searching for forbidden words.
entries.candidate_rule: Project subprocess creation remains centralized, shell-free, statically inspected, and role/argument allowlisted.
entries.governance_consequence: RF-A0.AUTHORITY.ALLOWLIST and CALL_SITES protect the execution boundary.
entries.open_question: The semantic trustworthiness of allowed tools remains an environmental limitation.

entries.observation: The canonical state and experiment schemas passed; SRF internal checks passed with NONE/NONE gate/evidence sentinels; the unchanged Praxis validator exited 1 at gate missing — NONE while HEAD remained absent.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; no current truthful pre-history representation satisfied the generic governed-project validator.
entries.interpretation: The former real gate/evidence paths semantically suggested prior verification despite NONE. Making all four sentinels honest improves SRF consistency but intentionally fails Praxis project validity earlier.
entries.learning: Schema validity, internal pre-history consistency, and governed-project validity are three different states in Praxis 0.1.
entries.candidate_rule: Do not fabricate prior gate/evidence/commit provenance; preserve the gap as a method candidate until Praxis evolves separately.
entries.open_question: Praxis must decide a canonical no-history representation outside this project.

entries.observation: Probe output, child handle, proc status, credentials, and executable link correlated for the live process.
entries.interpretation: Executable identity and live process identity are related but distinct.
entries.learning: A process claim needs live kernel state, not executable metadata alone.
entries.candidate_rule: Correlate process and executable through independent procfs observations.
entries.open_question: PID visibility under deliberate namespace variation belongs to RF-A2.

entries.observation: The reported regular descriptor resolved to the exact experiment file while the child lived.
entries.interpretation: The descriptor is process state distinct from the path.
entries.learning: File creation does not substitute for proving a retained live descriptor.
entries.candidate_rule: Correlate required regular resources through live descriptors.
entries.open_question: Rename, unlink, and persistence semantics belong to RF-A1.

entries.observation: Socket descriptor, inode, 127.0.0.1 LISTEN row, port, and active connection agreed.
entries.interpretation: Explicit binding evidence discriminates the result from a printed claim or external filter alone.
entries.learning: A listening endpoint is live socket state in a network context.

entries.observation: Launcher and child links matched for all ten namespace entries compared.
entries.interpretation: The relation shows inherited membership, not an absence of namespaces in the surrounding environment.
entries.learning: Namespace claims require an explicit comparison context.
entries.open_question: Namespace creation behavior belongs to RF-A2.

entries.observation: Launcher and child cgroup records matched byte-for-byte.
entries.interpretation: No project membership change was observed; this is not evidence of limits or controller governance.
entries.learning: Inherited membership and configured resource governance are distinct claims.
entries.candidate_rule: Report membership without claiming project-configured control.
entries.open_question: cgroup v2 controllers and limits belong to RF-A3.

entries.observation: The full run plus 128 immediate-after-ready collector iterations reported SIGTERM, controlled shutdown, zero exit, and no forced kill; CTest independently repeated 64 iterations.
entries.confrontation_with_prediction: SUPPORTED; no iteration contradicted the prediction.
entries.interpretation: Stress supports implementation behavior, while signal-mask/signalfd ordering explains removal of the identified race.
entries.learning: Controlled shutdown evidence combines notification mechanism, emitted state, bounded exit, status, and no forced termination.
entries.candidate_rule: Retain signalfd checks and bounded repetition without claiming mathematical proof.
entries.open_question: Crash recovery and production service lifecycle remain untested.
